title: Leading Up and Down the Chain of Command
coreMove: move context down and reality up before people act from different maps
sourcePressure: Leaders must explain purpose down the chain and communicate friction proactively up the chain so aligned initiative can continue.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

counterintuition: leadership is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: ask yourself how to be a better leader

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: railway maintenance night possession near a busy junction
exampleSpecs.audience: a track supervisor between field crew and operations center
exampleSpecs.stakes: field workers and dispatch can hold different pictures of when the track is safe
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor tells the crew the dispatch constraint, sends the ballast delay upward before it becomes hidden risk, and confirms the release time in both directions
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a track possession board glows in a trailer while rain dots the window

exampleSpecs.domain: zoo carnivore enclosure latch issue before public opening
exampleSpecs.audience: a keeper lead responsible to both keepers and the director
exampleSpecs.stakes: a small field concern can stay invisible above while keepers miss the reason for a closure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead explains to keepers why the exhibit stays closed, sends the exact latch risk and visitor-impact estimate upward, and asks for a clear opening decision
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are close enough to see this: red latch tag hangs from the snow leopard night gate.

exampleSpecs.domain: nonprofit canvass team hearing donor confusion about a policy change
exampleSpecs.audience: a field director leading canvassers and reporting to the executive team
exampleSpecs.stakes: the campaign can burn trust if donor confusion never travels upward
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director gives canvassers the purpose sentence, collects three exact donor objections on envelopes, and sends the pattern up with a recommended script change
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first thing you register is physical: three pledge envelopes carry the same question written in blue pen.

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital cafeteria substituting meals during a supplier shortage
exampleSpecs.audience: a food-service manager between procurement and dietary aides
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients with restrictions can receive wrong meals if purpose and constraints split
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager explains the shortage logic down to tray-line staff, sends allergy-risk concerns up to procurement, and changes the menu placard before lunch service
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Hold there," someone says. Menu placard lists turkey while the delivery crate holds only chicken.

exampleSpecs.domain: civil engineering inspection team finding sinkhole risk under a sidewalk
exampleSpecs.audience: a field engineer linking inspectors, city manager, and repair crew
exampleSpecs.stakes: senior leaders may underestimate risk while the repair crew misses the public-access reason
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the engineer sends soil-core photos and a closure recommendation upward, then explains to the crew why the detour must protect a senior-center entrance
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Later, the team will trace the lesson back to this: soil core tube comes up hollow at the edge of a cracked sidewalk panel.
mustAvoid: technical report as the whole communication

exampleSpecs.domain: software compliance deadline with a hidden vendor dependency
exampleSpecs.audience: a program manager between executives and implementation teams
exampleSpecs.stakes: executives see green while teams privately know the vendor export may arrive late
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager stops smoothing status, sends the vendor dependency upward with decision options, then tells teams which compliance promise still matters most
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes once this is in front of everyone: vendor export date sits blank on the audit calendar?

skillTargets: move purpose down and friction up the chain
recognize status smoothing and complaint framing as failures
choose the communication that protects aligned initiative

tryThisNowSpec: Write one purpose sentence that needs to travel down and one uncomfortable fact that needs to travel up before the next decision.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
